newsitem.title: UK: UK lobby wants windfall tax to avoid water users.
newsitem.headline: UK lobby wants windfall tax to avoid water users.

text.p: Britain's National Customer Council (NCC) for water industry regulator Ofwat on Friday called for the government to make companies and shareholders pay a proposed windfall tax instead of customers.
NCC said in a statement that it wanted legislation for the tax to be made "in such a way that the burden falls on the companies and their shareholders, not water customers."
The Labour government, which won power in a landslide victory on May 1, has vowed to introduce a one-off windfall tax on the "excess profits" of privatised utilities but has declined to give details.
"This tax could unfairly penalise water customers rather than the water companies and their shareholders," said NCC chairman Jim Gardiner.
He said the tax could "reduce the scope for the substantial and immediate cut in bills that NCC expects to see" at the next price review in 1999.
"The windfall tax will syphon off into general taxation money that belongs to water customers and should be returned to them in the form of lower bills," Gardiner said.
